sections.Aim and Purpose: Learn how to interrogate regulatory returns data critically, applying trend analysis and peer comparison rather than accepting figures at face value.
sections.Intended Audience: Mid-to-senior staff involved in building or using the authority's data/SupTech infrastructure.
Learning Objectives: Apply trend, ratio and peer analysis to regulatory returns
Identify inconsistencies between returns, financial statements and firm narratives
Formulate targeted supervisory questions from return analysis
Syllabus: Reading returns critically: what the numbers should and should not show
Trend analysis, ratios and peer group construction
Cross-checking returns against accounts, disclosures and other sources
Exercise: analysing a sample firm's returns and drafting follow-up questions
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some familiarity with suptech, data & supervisory analytics is helpful but not essential.
Core Reading: BIS Financial Stability Institute, Innovative Technology in Financial Supervision (Suptech): The Experience of Early Users (FSI Insights No 9, 2018)
FSB, The Use of Supervisory and Regulatory Technology by Authorities and Regulated Institutions (2020)
Basel Committee, Principles for Effective Risk Data Aggregation and Risk Reporting (BCBS 239) (2013)
